name: abduction of one leg flexion stretch
interpretation: One anatomical left knee fall-out from supine straight legs. The left knee first flexes, then opens out under control; the left foot slides toward the pelvis and rolls onto its external border. The opposite leg stays naturally extended and the pelvis remains level. Relaxed open hands rest palms upward alongside the body. Optional hand assistance is omitted. The source20–30second stretch hold is compressed to a clearly labeled1second demonstration hold; repeat mirrored for the other side.

instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bend one knee, let it fall out to the side and, if needed, ease it down with your hand until the inner thigh stretches.
Keep your lower back and the opposite hip flat on the floor.
Hold for 20-30 seconds, feeling a gentle pull rather than pain.
Release slowly and repeat, switching sides if the stretch is one sided.

explicit_staging.mirror_note: Repeat on the other side; this clip shows anatomical left only.
explicit_staging.hand_assistance: Omitted; source says if needed. No pulling or hand-knee contact is authored.
explicit_staging.hand_pose: Relaxed articulated fingers, palms up, backs of hands toward floor.
explicit_staging.pelvis: Fixed bone translation and orientation. A modest fixed posterior pelvic tilt and lumbar contour provide supine support without rolling.
explicit_staging.opposite_leg: Extended, small natural knee softness and slight external foot roll.
explicit_staging.active_foot: Illustrative heel slide during flexion and outer-border support during knee fall-out; source does not specify a planted sole.
explicit_staging.angles: Authored illustration, not source numerical ranges or clinical targets.
